recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-3318 unless the Security WG later undertakes a broader rewrite of FHIR access-control guidance or moves detailed implementation patterns to an IG.
issue_request: FHIR-3318 was a Published Security WG change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It requested text on security.html clarifying that FHIR supports RBAC because resources are object types and FHIR CRUDE events map to operations, and supports ABAC because resource instances can carry attributes including security tags, environment conditions, and user/object characteristics.
initial_application: The change appears to have been applied by b40621eca169838a924eb91eb5f77d5550622679, whose subject was "edit to add narrative on RBAC vs ABAC GF#3318" and which inserted the approved paragraphs into source/security.html. Later edits expanded the CRUDE acronym and made editorial/normative-wording cleanup while preserving the substance.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml actively lists secpriv-module.html with a Security child page filename="security.html", confirming build scope. Later Security WG issues FHIR-53717 and FHIR-53923 affected security.html wording but did not reverse or supersede the RBAC/ABAC guidance. Direct Confluence and Zulip searches for FHIR-3318 found no conflicting community record; broader RBAC/ABAC searches found implementation discussion only.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already contains the requested RBAC and ABAC explanation, including attributes beyond security tags, so adding more prose would be redundant rather than corrective.
